hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with 1,162 stops in four weeks
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break. He is also placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the office sees a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County. She recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, which has a 25 mph speed limit, his top stop was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and wants to make St. Lucie County a safer community. Local residents described seeing careless driving on the roads. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, said the situation is insane and that nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut others off. Del Toro emphasized that he cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones, stating he wants to make the community safer for all residents.

cards.headline: Donalds leads GOP primary as Collins challenges Fishback ballot eligibility in Florida governor's race
cards.body:
Republican congressman Byron Donalds maintains a commanding lead in the Florida governor's race as the August 18 primary approaches, with Democrat David Jolly consolidating support on the other side. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. Recent reports placed Collins' available resources at a fraction of that amount. President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary.

During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, arguing that Donalds could struggle in a general election. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and said the primary is a two-person race between himself and Donalds. Collins said his campaign has a clear path to victory despite trailing in polling, money and endorsements.

Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. Collins is challenging his eligibility to remain in the race, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, also announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign.

On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025 and involved fraudulent account statements and transfers through Govoni-controlled companies. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni also supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK in September
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. The carrier will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The optimism surrounding the launch contrasted sharply with the route's short lifespan, as the service failed to attract sufficient passenger numbers to remain viable.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The Boston service remains operational and provides ongoing connectivity for the region. However, the loss of the JFK route represents a setback for efforts to increase air service options at the smaller regional airport.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's statement indicated that all affected customers would receive full refunds for their cancelled flights as the carrier winds down operations on the route over the coming weeks.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff intensifies summer traffic crackdown after residents cite speeding, reckless driving
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. "I have a family that drives on these roadways. I care about my loved ones. I care about everyone else's loved ones. I want to make this a safer community," Del Toro said. Local residents including Ashley and Jessica say the problem is severe, with Ashley calling it "insane" and noting that nobody slows down. Jessica described drivers as careless and said they cut people off.

Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and is placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. "We see a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County," Benning said, adding that she most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described encountering a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed recorded there was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, representing a 155% increase.

The summer crackdown leverages available resources during the school break to address what residents have identified as a pressing safety concern on county roads. By redeploying school resource officers to traffic duties and assigning high-performing deputies to problem areas, the sheriff's office aims to curb dangerous driving behaviors that have become commonplace on local roadways. The dramatic increase in citations under Del Toro's leadership reflects his commitment to making traffic enforcement a priority across the agency rather than limiting it to a specialized unit.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. Funding comes from local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

The tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and nine at the school during Hurricane Milton. However, Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already scheduled to receive construction work before the hurricane hit. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," Gernaine said. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

Students displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out of the construction area.

The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The reconstruction represents a combination of previously planned improvements and necessary repairs from the hurricane damage, allowing the school to move forward with both projects simultaneously.

cards.headline: JetBlue Cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK Route After Nine Months, Cites Low Demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. In a statement to WPTV, JetBlue said demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by the airline and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to those who had hoped the direct connection would provide a more convenient travel option for the region.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport's efforts to attract additional airline service have met with mixed results, as the cancellation of the JFK route demonstrates the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining new routes. The Boston service remains in place, providing at least one direct connection to a major northeastern city for Treasure Coast travelers.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's decision to end the route after just nine months highlights the difficulty of predicting passenger demand for new regional routes, even when initial enthusiasm suggests strong potential. The continuation of the Boston service indicates JetBlue remains committed to serving the Vero Beach market, though at a reduced capacity compared to when both routes were operational.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents return to St. Lucie County condos after nearly 2 years of displacement
cards.teaser: Residents of Villa Del Sol in St. Lucie County are returning home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos following structural damage that forced evacuations in August 2024.
cards.body:
Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos after nearly two years of displacement. An inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share with WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return. WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they are still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe and that he and his family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she feels bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

hero.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
hero.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee, last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine each found their way to gymnastics through different paths but now compete as one unit on the national stage. Head Coach Candice Lazuka described the season as strong, with the team competing locally before traveling to states and regionals.

At AAU Nationals, the trio came close to achieving a perfect score during their routines. The team earned a 9.9 score, narrowly missing a perfect 10. Lazuka explained that achieving a perfect 10 is difficult. The strong performance at nationals qualified the gymnasts for the Junior Olympics competition in Iowa, scheduled for next month.

The gymnasts expressed excitement about their upcoming competition. Rose-Daris said she is looking forward to traveling to an entirely different part of the world. Supan described the qualification as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said her focus heading into the Junior Olympics is getting first place on floors.

Each gymnast came to the sport through a different path. Rose-Daris said it started not really with gymnastics itself but with the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. Despite their different starting points, the three young athletes have come together as a team and are now preparing to represent Flip City Gym and Cheer at one of the most prestigious competitions in youth gymnastics.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 in World Cup semifinal after late rally
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinal, advancing to the final against Spain on Sunday.
cards.body:
Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday in the World Cup semifinal, scoring both goals in the final minutes of the match. England took the lead when Anthony Gordon scored in the 55th minute, but Enzo Fernandez swept in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winning goal two minutes into stoppage time from a cross by Lionel Messi. Martinez said he told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he was going to come on and win it. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff and the fans, and that the players gave every bit of blood, sweat and tears.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team was ready to go home sad after England scored, but they really proved themselves. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm while England played with a feeling that they have a lot to lose. The loss marked the third time England came up short in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 victory over France
cards.teaser: Spain will face either Argentina or England in the World Cup final Sunday after defeating France 2-0 in the semifinal on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot in the 22nd minute after teenager Lamine Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, who was playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Pedro Porro added a second goal in the 58th minute on a give-and-go with Dani Olmo. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament.

Yamal, a day after his 19th birthday, was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's goal. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. France, FIFA's top-ranked team, will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium. This win marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match. Yamal scored in a 2-1 win in the 2024 European Championship semifinals just days before his 17th birthday, and Spain won 5-4 in Nations League play last year.

cards.headline: Florida Panthers to open 2026-27 NHL season on four-game road trip starting with defending champion Carolina
cards.teaser: The Panthers will begin their regular season on Sept. 29 against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes before their home opener Oct. 11 against Minnesota Wild.
cards.body:
The Florida Panthers are set to begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season campaign on the road, taking on four Western Conference opponents. The Panthers will open against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29, marking a marquee matchup to begin the year. The road trip continues with stops in San Jose on Oct. 6. After their four-game road swing, the Cats will return to South Florida for their highly anticipated home opener on Saturday, Oct. 11, when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena.

December will be particularly busy with seven home games, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. One of those games is Dec. 27 against the Buffalo Sabres. Fans will enjoy two consecutive five-game homestands during the season. The first runs Dec. 19-30 and the second from March 2-12.

cards.headline: England and Argentina renew historic World Cup rivalry in semifinal
cards.teaser: The two nations meet Wednesday in Atlanta with a spot in the World Cup final against Spain on the line, continuing a rivalry dating back to 1962.
cards.body:
England and Argentina resume one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta, with the winner playing Spain in the final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday. The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but it intensified with England's 1-0 win in the quarterfinals in 1966. Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced on Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. England went on to win the World Cup for the first, and still the only time, in its history. Twenty years later in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 win in the quarterfinals on the way to becoming world champion for a second time. That game also saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said anybody who loves football will remember that in the best way possible.

Neither team has had a smooth ride to the semifinals. Argentina survived scares against Cape Verde and Egypt earlier in the knockout rounds and needed extra time to beat 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in the quarterfinals. England had to rally for wins against Congo and Norway after going a goal down and endured a physically exhausting game played at altitude while being down to 10 men to beat co-host Mexico 3-2 in the round of 16.

cards.headline: Atlanta increases security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal amid clash concerns
cards.teaser: Police will increase personnel and resources for Wednesday's match after videos showed England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami over the weekend.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match.

Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is also the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals. Argentina has claimed three World Cup titles and been the tournament's runner-up twice.

cards.headline: World Cup semifinals set with England, Argentina, France and Spain reaching final four
cards.teaser: The four highest-ranked teams advanced to the semifinals after England and Argentina won quarterfinal matches over the weekend.
cards.body:
The World Cup's final four is set with England, Argentina, France and Spain advancing to the semifinals after quarterfinal matches over the weekend. England defeated Norway with Jude Bellingham scoring twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. The 23-year-old has been everywhere on the pitch for England throughout the tournament. Argentina advanced past Switzerland after striker Julián Alvarez scored in extra time, with help from a controversial VAR call. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition for England. Argentina has scored the most goals out of anyone in the tournament with 17 and has relied on Lionel Messi to get the team out of trouble, though Alvarez was the star in the quarterfinal. Many members of Argentina's current squad won the World Cup title in 2022. England was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018 but lost to Croatia. The country is looking for its first World Cup title since 1966.

France has barely gotten out of first gear so far this summer, relying on Kylian Mbappé and Ousmane Dembélé in its front line. Legendary manager Didier Deschamps is leaving his role after this tournament. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament and will face France in the semifinal. Spain beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024 and also beat France in the Nations League last year. Whoever wins the France-Spain semifinal will likely be favorite to win the whole thing on July 19.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to nearly 1,250 children through Summer BreakSpot program
hero.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children.
hero.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is helping provide thousands of free meals to children this summer through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization said it supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, the organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed.

During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, Palm Beach County Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. Chef Doug Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. Jamie Kendall said the Food Bank's partnership with Summer BreakSpot helps ensure children continue receiving nutritious meals while school is out. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, announces new koala joey named Bonza
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10 and announced that its newest koala joey is a boy named Bonza.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. The zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, said the name is Aussie slang for awesome or excellent. Zoo staff members from departments ranging from accounting to marketing helped document and share the koala family's journey with the public.

Palm Beach Zoo announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. July's event will also serve as an early preview of this year's Zoo Lights celebration. Joiner said guests can expect new lighting displays, updated activations and a noticeably different experience compared to previous years.

hero.headline: Donalds leads GOP primary as Collins challenges Fishback ballot eligibility in Florida governor's race
hero.body:
Republican congressman Byron Donalds maintains a commanding lead in the Florida governor's race as the August 18 primary approaches, with Democrat David Jolly consolidating support on the other side. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. Recent reports placed Collins' available resources at a fraction of that amount. President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary.

During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, arguing that Donalds could struggle in a general election. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and said the primary is a two-person race between himself and Donalds. Collins said his campaign has a clear path to victory despite trailing in polling, money and endorsements.

Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. Collins is challenging his eligibility to remain in the race, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, also announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign.

On the Democratic side, Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025 and involved fraudulent account statements and transfers through Govoni-controlled companies. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni also supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers homeowners rates by 5.6% for Florida customers
cards.teaser: The Ormond Beach-based insurer is reducing rates and launching a disappearing deductible program that rewards claims-free customers.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as customers don't have a loss. Once a loss occurs, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County as the district launches a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The project includes rebuilding structures destroyed by the tornadoes, along with constructing a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a complete parking lot overhaul. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

The school was already scheduled for construction work when the hurricane struck. The tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and nine, which were then added to the existing renovation plans. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

Students displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out of the construction area.

The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The combination of previously planned improvements and hurricane damage repairs has created a comprehensive rebuilding project for the middle school campus.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff intensifies summer traffic crackdown after residents cite speeding, reckless driving
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. "I have a family that drives on these roadways. I care about my loved ones. I care about everyone else's loved ones. I want to make this a safer community," Del Toro said. Local residents including Ashley and Jessica say the problem is severe, with Ashley calling it "insane" and noting that nobody slows down. Jessica described drivers as careless and said they cut people off.

Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and is placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern. Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. "We see a lot of excessive speeding in St. Lucie County," Benning said, adding that she most recently had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues described encountering a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed recorded there was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, representing a 155% increase.

The summer crackdown leverages available resources during the school break to address what residents have identified as a pressing safety concern on county roads. By redeploying school resource officers to traffic duties and assigning high-performing deputies to problem areas, the sheriff's office aims to curb dangerous driving behaviors that have become commonplace on local roadways. The dramatic increase in citations under Del Toro's leadership reflects his commitment to making traffic enforcement a priority across the agency rather than limiting it to a specialized unit.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
cards.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
cards.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: JetBlue Cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK Route After Nine Months, Cites Low Demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. In a statement to WPTV, JetBlue said demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by the airline and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to those who had hoped the direct connection would provide a more convenient travel option for the region.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport's efforts to attract additional airline service have met with mixed results, as the cancellation of the JFK route demonstrates the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining new routes. The Boston service remains in place, providing at least one direct connection to a major northeastern city for Treasure Coast travelers.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's decision to end the route after just nine months highlights the difficulty of predicting passenger demand for new regional routes, even when initial enthusiasm suggests strong potential. The continuation of the Boston service indicates JetBlue remains committed to serving the Vero Beach market, though at a reduced capacity compared to when both routes were operational.

cards.headline: JetBlue Cancels JFK to Vero Beach Flights Creating Tourism Challenge
cards.teaser: The cancellation of JetBlue's JFK to Vero Beach route creates new challenges for Treasure Coast tourism connectivity.
cards.body:
JetBlue's decision to end direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach after nine months creates a challenge for Florida's Treasure Coast tourism connectivity. Low passenger demand forced the airline to cancel the route.

The cancellation affects traveler access between New York and the Treasure Coast region. The route had been viewed as an important connection for the area's tourism industry.
